questions.question_text:
Symbol meanings: @ means >; % means ≤; # means <; & means >=; ^ means =;

Statement: K & H @ U @ L ^ G % P # J ^ N

Conclusions:
I. N # L
II. K @ G
III. H % J

Question: Which of the listed conclusions logically follow?
questions.explanation: The chain gives K≥H>U>L=G≤P<J=N. II (K>G) is forced; I is false because N>L; III (H≤J) is not forced.
questions.source: PDF: Inequality 01  Class Notes.pdf.pdf; physical page(s) 3

questions.question_text:
Symbol meanings: # means ≤; $ means >; % means =; & means <; @ means >=;

Statement: A # Y % B & E @ S @ G

Conclusions:
I. G @ A
II. Y # E

Question: Which of the listed conclusions logically follow?
questions.explanation: The chain is A≤Y=B<E and E≥S≥G. Thus Y<E, so II follows; G≥A is not entailed.
questions.source: PDF: Inequality 01  Class Notes.pdf.pdf; physical page(s) 4

questions.question_text:
Symbol meanings: @ means <; # means >; % means =; $ means >=; Ω means ≤;

Statement: R # J @ S Ω B @ D % F $ C Ω H # K $ T

Conclusions:
I. D @ T
II. F $ T
III. J $ F

Question: Which of the listed conclusions logically follow?

options.B: Either I or II is true
options.C: Both I and II are true
options.D: Both I and III are true

questions.explanation: The chain yields R>J, J<S≤B<D=F, F≥C≤H<K and K≥T. Neither D<T nor F≥T is forced. J<S≤B<D=F proves J<F, contradicting III.
questions.source: PDF: Inequality 01  Class Notes.pdf.pdf; physical page(s) 5

questions.question_text:
Symbol meanings: @ means >; % means ≤; # means <; & means >=; ^ means =;

Statement: S ^ T # U % V & W @ X

Conclusions:
I. S # V
II. T & W
III. X # S

Question: Which of the listed conclusions logically follow?

options.D: Both conclusions ii and iii follow

questions.explanation: S=T<U≤V and W>X. Thus S<V, so I follows. The other comparisons are not entailed.
questions.source: PDF: Inequality 02  Class Notes.pdf; physical page(s) 6

questions.question_text:
Symbol meanings: & means =; % means <; $ means >; @ means ≤; # means >=;

Statement: A % B & C @ D # E & F

Conclusions:
I. A & E
II. D $ A
III. C # F

Question: Which of the listed conclusions logically follow?

options.D: Both conclusions ii and iii follow

questions.explanation: A<B=C≤D≥E=F. II (D>A) follows because D≥C=B>A. I is not forced and C≥F is not forced.
questions.source: PDF: Inequality 02  Class Notes.pdf; physical page(s) 9

questions.question_text:
Symbol meanings: & means =; % means <; $ means >; @ means ≤; # means >=;

Statement: A $ B & C, C & D # E % F

Conclusions:
I. A & E
II. C & E
III. B # D

Question: Which of the listed conclusions logically follow?

options.D: Both conclusions ii and iii follow

questions.explanation: A>B=C=D≥E and E<F. Equality conclusions I and II do not follow; B=D makes III true under # (≥).
questions.source: PDF: Inequality 02  Class Notes.pdf; physical page(s) 10

questions.question_text:
Symbol meanings: $ means =; & means <; % means >; # means ≤; @ means >=;

Statement: T $ U % V, W # X $ V % Y

Conclusions:
I. T % X
II. U # Y
III. W # Y

Question: Which of the listed conclusions logically follow?

options.D: Both conclusions ii and iii follow

questions.explanation: T=U>V=X>Y and W≤X. I (T>X) follows; II is false, while W≤Y is not entailed.
questions.source: PDF: Inequality 02  Class Notes.pdf; physical page(s) 13
